context: A conceptual git question: explain the lease check and its background-fetch gap, without touching any repository or change request.

checklist.name: Lease explained
checklist.description: Says the push is refused when the remote branch no longer matches the value the local remote-tracking ref (or an explicit expected value) records, unlike --force, which overwrites unconditionally.

checklist.name: Gap named
checklist.description: Explains that a fetch after the other person's push (for example a background fetch by an editor) updates the tracking ref, so the lease passes and their commits are overwritten.

checklist.name: Mitigation
checklist.description: Mentions --force-if-includes, or passing an explicit expected commit to --force-with-lease, as the guard for that case.

checklist.name: No live actions
checklist.description: Runs no push, opens or edits no pull request, and does not turn the answer into a change-request workflow.
